How to travel cheap
and still live well
Travel in shoulder season. Late spring and early autumn mean lower prices, fewer crowds and better weather than you'd expect. The same trip can cost half as much.
Eat where the locals eat. Walk two streets away from the main square. The food is better, the prices are fairer and you'll often end up chatting with people who live there.
Stay in neighbourhoods, not tourist centres. A short metro ride saves a lot of money, and you see how people really live in the city instead of a postcard version of it.
Walk everywhere you can. It's free, it's healthy and it's the best way to discover a city. Some of the best places you'll find were never in any guide.
Learn the story of a place before you go. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and every city I visit means more because I know its past.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Every city I visit means more because I know its past.

slides.texte_overlay: Pack light. One carry-on bag saves fees, time and stress. You need far fewer clothes than you think, and moving around becomes so much easier.
Spend on experiences, save on things. A boat trip or a cooking class stays with you for years. Souvenirs usually end up in a drawer.
